facts.text: The collected official website markets mattresses, sofas, recliners, beds, pillows, accessories and smart sleep solutions in India.
Duroflex's official Our Story page traces its beginnings to Kerala in 1963; this is the brand's own historical account.
The official article dated 28 November 2025 announces Designed to De-Stress as Duroflex's new philosophy.
The supplied Strategic Blueprint defines Motivating Reset as the brand essence and an attentive, insightful, supportive and warm personality; these are strategic intentions.
The supplied Visual World Guide contains 151 slides and remains draft, including pages labelled approved, mandatory or locked and its approval scorecard.

Restore, Recharge, Oasis and Recalibrate appear in proposed strategy architecture, while collected navigation retains other range names. Adoption of the complete proposed architecture is not established.

Official supplied imagery uses a solid symbol and uppercase DUROFLEX; the draft renders a lowercase serif wordmark and older tagline despite requesting sans-serif typography. Final production masters are unresolved.

guardian.preferences.text: Proposal, not approved guidance: explore contemporary, tactile domestic settings where architecture, circulation and light make room for pausing, connecting and participating again. Treat the draft guide and reference interiors as inspiration, not specifications.

The draft proposes warm neutrals with selected deeper or natural tones and tactile surfaces. These are exploratory relationships, not approved swatches, material specifications or a requirement to make every scene beige.

Official imagery shows a red symbol and uppercase DUROFLEX; treat this as observed identity, not a complete production specification. Confirm approved logo, lockup and typography rather than reconstructing them from draft slides.
Draft proposal: favor believable domestic actions and relaxed contact over presenter-like posing. Casting, wardrobe and gestures remain creative choices, not approved mandatory rules.
The official site shows varied category and promotional treatments. These are dated examples of current practice, not a permanent visual system or a requirement to imitate sale styling.

brandResearch.findings.title: Research coverage is extensive; this refresh is a representative review
brandResearch.findings.text: The separate Astra study records 371 image inspections across 11 requests: 151 draft-guide slides, 106 visible positioning slides, 58 unique interior references and 56 website images from 12 official pages. This refresh uses those indexed interpretations plus eight actually supplied image previews—not a second inspection of all 371 images. The two research documents are derived model analysis, not newly approved guidelines. All 151 visual-guide slides remain draft, including the locked-character caption and approval scorecard. Stored-only images receive no inspected labels here.

brandResearch.findings.title: Sleep heritage is expanding into a broader comfort proposition
brandResearch.findings.text: The official Our Story page traces Duroflex to Kerala in 1963 and describes expansion beyond mattresses into furniture and accessories. The supplied positioning defines the essence as Motivating Reset. The official article dated 28 November 2025 announces Designed to De-Stress and an evolution from sleep brand to science-backed comfort brand. These establish heritage and intended positioning; they do not independently validate stress treatment, physiological recovery or product efficacy.

brandResearch.findings.title: Public identity has changed; draft logo and typography remain unresolved
brandResearch.findings.text: The supplied official logo and homepage show a solid red symbol with uppercase DUROFLEX. W03 announces Designed to De-Stress; its indexed old/new comparison records the earlier Great Sleep. Great Health. identity. The inspected draft V018 instead displays lowercase serif duroflex and Better Sleep / A Brighter You, while V086 requests clean sans-serif hierarchy. Font substitution may contribute but is not established. Confirm production vectors, typography and tagline lockups rather than reconstructing them from slides; retain authentic branding already present on the selected product.

brandResearch.findings.title: Red signals recognition, but its environmental boundary is contradictory
brandResearch.findings.text: Draft V035 and V087 make red identification rather than an all-red room: logo, product tag, CTA or a restrained graphic anchor. The indexed review nevertheless records red shorts, bedding, cushions and throws in positive examples, whereas V128 prohibits red outfits, bedding and props while permitting a single object. This is an unresolved draft contradiction, not automatic permission. The homepage confirms red identity and interface accents, but supplies no authoritative colour values. Keep immutable product colour separate from optional styling and resolve environmental red before production.

brandResearch.findings.title: Let architecture and circulation create calm
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed application: plan the entrance, openings, product footprint, storage, activity zone and passage before choosing décor. The inspected R20 reference integrates a workstation and mirror with a bedroom; V018 relates low furniture to broad openings, wall planes and recessed storage. Borrow legible domestic organisation rather than copying reference furniture. Keep bedside access and seating approaches usable, with tables outside verified extension paths. Reserve genuine wall and floor space without making the product tiny. Spatial clarity communicates an impression of ease, not demonstrated stress reduction.

brandResearch.findings.title: Material and colour relationships matter more than beige minimalism
brandResearch.findings.text: The draft proposes bone, sand, taupe and stone alongside sage, olive, clay, wine, midnight blue and soft sky. Inspected R20 contrasts sage walls, darker timber outlines and pale textiles; R36 layers timber-looking planes, neutral bedding and directional light. V018 adds texture and greenery rather than colourlessness. These support tonal separation and tactile variety, not approved swatches or authenticated material composition. Product colour must remain unchanged; room surfaces should support it rather than force every category into one neutral palette.

brandResearch.findings.title: Make light explain the room and camera explain use
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed production approach: establish one credible principal light source, supported by believable practical lamps. R36 visibly connects left glazing to wall and floor shadows. Use frontal framing for silhouette, three-quarter views for depth and circulation, and close views for contact and construction. Preserve SKU colour, fabric grain and floor contact rather than adding a warm cast everywhere. The draft names morning, quiet-day and evening modes, but the indexed review finds repeated daylight examples under evening headings; intended time therefore needs separate lighting references, not assumption from captions.

brandResearch.findings.title: Direct supported actions, natural contact and relaxed wardrobe
brandResearch.findings.text: The draft favours reading, turning, reclining, stretching and companionship over presenter poses or forced smiles. Proposed direction: check pelvis, back, head, feet, hands, cushion compression, occlusion and garment tension together. Use relaxed, matte, tactile homewear with enough tonal contrast to reveal contact; the draft suggests linen, washed cotton, jersey and muted colours. Indian relevance is a casting intention, not something to infer from faces. The indexed character appendix includes fashion-like poses and lustrous clothing that do not consistently match these instructions; its locked caption remains draft.

brandResearch.findings.title: Six room families provide a flexible—not mandatory—spatial menu
brandResearch.findings.text: Derived proposals: (1) Compact connected home—integrate sleep, storage and a modest work/activity zone. (2) Garden-threshold reset—use framed greenery, low horizons and an accessible outdoor edge. (3) Filtered-light contemporary room—borrow screen depth without transplanting a complete themed interior. (4) Warm social lounge—make conversation and seating extension legible. (5) Sheltered reading/recovery corner—provide reachable light, controls and a clear approach. (6) Colour-led bedroom—use one restrained wall/recess tone around the unchanged SKU. These are advisory translations from the indexed references, not six approved sets; avoid resort spectacle, obstructive benches and accumulated ornament.

brandResearch.findings.title: Mattresses: one domestic foundation, distinct Airboost and Duropedic treatments
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed mattress world: a usable bedroom with opening-led daylight, bedside storage and enough exposed edge, quilting and branding to identify the variant. Airboost can use restrained blue-white freshness and a separately verified technical view—not a blue cast, floating mattress or invented cutaway. Duropedic can express human trust through warm domestic architecture and supported everyday rest—not medical theatre, pain grimaces or anatomical glows. The indexed official selection includes ornate bedroom settings; retain product clarity without inheriting chandeliers or hotel staging. Turning, reading and waking are narrative actions, not airflow or orthopedic proof.

brandResearch.findings.title: Sofas and motion: social release with accurate mechanics
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed direction: build a connected conversation or entertainment zone rather than a matching showroom set. Let the exact upholstery colour lead against quieter architecture; use natural, independent postures for shared reading or conversation. Develop daylight and practical-lit evening versions separately. For motion products, pair the closed silhouette with a verified extended configuration and supported use, keeping tables and people clear of the mechanism. Ports, motors and reclining geometry must come from the selected model, not another sofa or collection-wide copy. This interprets the draft's Evening Exhale mood without making every lounge dark.

brandResearch.findings.title: Recliners: a personal pause within an accessible home
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed recliner setting: a sheltered reading corner with reachable lighting, a usable approach and visible support for arms, back and lower legs. Selectively deeper wall tones can frame the chair without hiding upholstery or controls. The indexed study contrasts transferable domestic settings with floral coastal arches; borrow enclosure and chair visibility, not resort scenery. Show only the selected chair's documented positions and operation. Category placement or a resting pose cannot establish rocking, rotation, powered adjustment, therapeutic benefit or outdoor suitability.

brandResearch.findings.title: Beds and smart sleep: distinguish architectural form from function
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed approach: decide whether the bed frame, mattress or complete combination is the hero. Give upholstered beds readable headboard shape, fabric and room access; demonstrate storage separately where documented. For smart sleep, distinguish mattress firmness adjustment from bed articulation, and show only a verified compatible combination. Reading, preparing for bed or getting up provides domestic context. Bedding that conceals articulation cannot demonstrate adjustment. The indexed sage-and-clay bedroom treatment is one useful precedent, not a universal bed palette or proof of the product labels' portfolio status.

brandResearch.findings.title: Pillows and accessories: close, specific contact rather than generic softness
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed Micro Restoration treatment: intimate bedside context, touch and clearly visible surface detail. Match head contact, adjustment or seated use to the actual pillow form; preserve contour, edging and pattern. For toppers, protectors and comforters, make the selected item identifiable rather than allowing styling to hide it. The indexed website examples mix dark graphics, blue use scenes and yellow packaging, so no single accessory palette is established. Appearance and poses cannot substantiate loft, fibre composition, cooling, alignment or health outcomes.

brandResearch.findings.title: Massagers: explain technology through correct domestic use
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed recovery world: a warm, functional corner with clear device access, grounded contact and understandable controls—neither spa spectacle nor clinic. The draft includes a domestic foot-device precedent, whereas the indexed official visuals commonly isolate devices on dark fields. Supplement form recognition with documented seated use, keeping open and closed configurations distinct. Do not invent body contact, heat glows, treatment durations or device capabilities. Clinical and healing language on W11 is current marketing copy, not independent substantiation or permission to depict medical outcomes.

brandResearch.findings.title: Extend the story from pause to participation, including retail
brandResearch.findings.text: Proposed narrative: arrival, settling, connection and readiness—not an entire campaign of closed eyes. Reading, conversation, hobbies or preparing to join others can express Motivating Reset without promising a product-caused transformation. In retail, translate the supplied strategy into arrival, attentive consultation, semi-private trials and unwind/social zones with unobstructed access. A decorative niche does not demonstrate a working store. Keep the experience neither clinical nor a luxury spa, and connect bedroom and lounge worlds through spatial logic rather than identical décor.

brandResearch.findings.title: Build a source-shot system with product integrity as the first gate
brandResearch.findings.text: Use the draft's World, Icon, Inhabited Hero and Intelligence classes as provisional planning prompts, then derive channel and sale layouts. Preserve the exact product's colour, construction, seams, labels and controls; check shared light, shadows, anatomy, contact and verified clearances before aesthetic review. Texture documents appearance, not composition or efficacy. Reconcile V065's four classes with V150's broader deliverables, and correct V151: eight ten-point criteria accompany a claimed total of 100. Neither its score nor any mandatory wording establishes approval.

brandResearch.findings.title: Proposed portfolio architecture is not the collected navigation
brandResearch.findings.text: Positioning P063 proposes folding Livein and Natural Living into a simplified architecture; P066–P074 develop Restore, Recharge, Oasis and Recalibrate and an expanded Neuma world. The later official navigation still retains multiple mattress ranges and overlapping routes. Proposed trackers, apps, masks and other future concepts are not proof of current availability. A Restore label reported on a product image does not establish adoption of the whole architecture. Obtain the adopted naming and migration map before changing public range names or assigning new product stories.

brandResearch.findings.title: Strategy claims and website claims do not constitute approved SKU proof
brandResearch.findings.text: P053 uses 200K strands, 4X airflow and pain/stress-release language; collected website copy uses one lakh-plus fibres and 3X breathability. These are not established like-for-like comparisons, so choosing the newer number would not resolve them. W11 and W12 also contain broad healing, circulation and recovery language. Treat these as attributed marketing statements, not independently validated effects. Medical, cortisol, pain-relief, stress-treatment, quantified-performance and guarantee claims require current, product-specific approved evidence. Customer counts and qualitative consumer observations likewise do not establish population statistics.

brandResearch.findings.title: Current selling intensity and dark technology treatments coexist with draft calm
brandResearch.findings.text: The inspected homepage screenshot combines black-and-gold Great Comfort Fest graphics, red gift plinths, a countdown and offer-led information with diverse category thumbnails. The indexed study also records dark Neuma staging and richer motion-sofa scenes. These document current executions, not permanent rules overriding the draft's warm domestic ambition. Keep commercial panels distinct from room photography and revalidate offers. W11 itself conflicts: product cards show 4–20% discounts while body copy promotes flat 50% launch deals; this cannot be carried into a fresh brief unresolved.

brandResearch.findings.title: Graphic gradients do not permit fabricated photographic backgrounds
brandResearch.findings.text: Draft V089–V090 propose rounded panels and subtle atmospheric gradients. The configured client scene-integration boundary prohibits fake white patches, contrast fades, haze, blur masks and gradients inside photographs. Draft examples and observed website treatments do not override that boundary. Use genuine architectural copy space or a clearly separate graphic canvas, with any graphic treatment subject to approval. Likewise, retouching language about distracting labels must not be read as permission to remove authentic product branding.

brandResearch.findings.title: Close production and research gaps before execution
brandResearch.findings.text: Select the exact official SKU, variant, channel and approved claim set before commissioning scenes. Confirm logo masters, typography, portfolio adoption and reference-reuse permissions; obtain dimensions or mechanism requirements wherever the composition needs them. Occupied massager and adjustable-bed sequences remain comparatively thin in the indexed study, and motion/video continuity was not reviewed. Social accounts are linked but their creative feeds are not established here. Meta access returned 403 and advertiser identity was not verified; no paid-creative, targeting, performance or audience conclusions follow.
